evidence: STATIC DESIGN (no task-specific inversion found): tests/scoring.toml, tests/tools/score.py and tests/test.sh are byte-identical to the frozen template (diff clean); scoring.toml gates render/constraints=0.0, weights functional 0.6/polish 0.2/visual 0.2, floors functional=0.05. score.py:41 gates_passed=all(score>0.0); :47-48 reward=weighted only if gates and floors pass. Functional dominates mass (0.6). Gates (tests/gates/render/judge.toml:23, constraints/judge.toml:23) demand only publicly required behaviour (sign-in refusal+valid sign-in; recruiter opens job with team/manager/2 places and adds candidate; independent Observer context sees it — hireops_rules.md §1 Observer 'reads the board', §2) with an 'another working staff account is acceptable' fallback, so a stronger conforming app is not plausibly gated out. Each scored prompt repeats the same gate (functional/prompt.md:11-13, polish/prompt.md:11-12, visual/prompt.md:11-12), consistent with the gate suite. Functional: 43 binary criteria, weight sum 58.5 (0.5..2.5); heaviest rows are concurrency/privacy/live (hro_stale_refused 2.5, hro_candidate_private 2.5, hro_live_board 2.5), lightest are trivial intake (hro_job_open 0.5, hro_add_candidate 0.5), so weights rise with difficulty/importance. Every refusal row names a positive control (e.g. hro_undo_full:127 'other successful undos ... are the control', hro_activity_refusals:271, hro_observer_readonly:173, hro_candidate_private:389 'receives none of its own data is 0'), so a dead/no-op app cannot outscore a working one via negatives. functional/prompt.md:13 scores rows independently and re-sets up failed steps on a new job, and :23 'Never deduct one observed defect in more than one row', limiting cascade inversions. Floor 0.05 = 2.925 of 58.5 weight: a gate-passing app with only intake rows (job_open+add_candidate=1.0 -> 0.017) scores 0, so a pretty near-stub cannot farm visual 0.2. Polish (weight sum 12) is behavioural (live preservation, earlier-place anchoring, failed send, session resume) — all public (instruction.md:5,7; rules §5,§6); its live rows are 0 when no live update arrives (polish/judge.toml:23,32), which compounds with hro_live_board but in the correct direction. Visual: 5 likert(5) rows weight 1.2 each with anchors; gate failure -> Likert 1 -> 0. MISSING/UNMEASURED: raw-evidence-index.json 'scope' states 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent'; only a scripted golden driver exists (not a judge run). REVIEW_POLICY.md:31 requires hash-bound runtime records for reward ordering before clearance. Residual budget-driven inversion is plausible and unmeasured: functional judge timeout=9000 s (functional/judge.toml:4) for 43 criteria across 14 protocols (Z,S,M,L,C,B,N,T,U,K,R,V,A,D) with many independent contexts and 15 s waits; polish timeout=900 s for gate setup + 5 multi-context rows. test.sh run_suite (timeout 11100 for scored; 9000+900+900=10800 nests) — if the functional judge exceeds its budget and rewardkit errors, test.sh 'if ! run_suite scored 11100; then exit 0' leaves the plain zero; and prompts instruct 'NOT EXERCISED' -> binary 0 for budget-exhausted rows (functional/prompt.md:53). A fully working app exercises every protocol step (longest walk) while a broken app short-circuits, so the better app is the one more exposed to timeout/zero. Whether harbor-rewardkit 0.1.7 fails the whole suite or returns partial scores on judge timeout was not verifiable locally (package not inspected).
counterexample: Not a demonstrated Fail; unmeasured risk scenario: App G (golden-like, every feature works) makes the functional judge walk all 14 protocols and exceed timeout=9000 s or exhaust budget before V/A/D, yielding plain zero or 0 on hro_live_board(2.5)/hro_activity/hro_restart(1.5); App W (bulk move, undo and conversations broken) short-circuits B/T/U and finishes within budget with functional ~0.4 and positive reward — W outscores G. Conforming alternative that could fail: a correct app whose live-update interval is 14 s makes every U/V/polish wait reach the 15 s ceiling, lengthening the run further.
suggested_fix: Produce hash-bound full configured verifier runs on the golden plus at least two mutated weaker apps (e.g. no undo/bulk; no live updates) recording judge duration per suite and final rewards, confirm golden > weaker ordering and functional judge duration well under 9000 s; if not, cut protocol scope rather than auto-raising budgets.
